company.name: Aurora Lithium Corp.
company.tagline: Powering the Battery Supply Chain of Tomorrow
company.description: is a TSX Venture listed exploration and development company advancing a portfolio of lithium brine projects across the Lithium Triangle of South America. The company combines district-scale land positions with a disciplined, drill-driven exploration strategy targeting near-term resource definition.

highlights.title: Critical Commodity
highlights.text: Lithium demand is forecast to triple by 2035, driven by EV adoption and grid-scale storage buildout.

highlights.title: District Scale
highlights.text: Over 48,000 hectares across two salars in the Lithium Triangle, host to more than half of global lithium resources.

highlights.title: Drill-Ready Targets
highlights.text: Fully permitted 5,000 m drill program underway with first resource estimate targeted for Q1 2027.

highlights.title: Proven Team
highlights.text: Leadership with multiple discoveries and exits in South American brine and hard-rock lithium projects.

highlights.title: Funded Through 2027
highlights.text: $11.4M treasury fully funds current drill campaigns and maiden resource publication.

highlights.title: Low-Impact DLE
highlights.text: Piloting direct lithium extraction to cut water consumption versus conventional evaporation ponds.

projects.name: Salar Grande Project
projects.summary: Flagship brine project covering 31,000 ha in the heart of the Lithium Triangle.
bullets: Historic sampling up to 540 mg/L lithium with low magnesium ratios
Phase 1 drilling intersected brine-bearing aquifers over 180 m thickness
Adjacent to producing operations with established infrastructure access

projects.name: Cerro Blanco Project
projects.summary: Earlier-stage 17,000 ha salar position with surface samples grading up to 380 mg/L lithium.
bullets: Geophysics completed; maiden drill targets defined for H2 2026
Road-accessible, 40 km from rail and power corridor

news.title: Phase 1 drilling confirms thick brine horizons at Salar Grande
Closes $6.5M bought-deal financing led by institutional investors
